body:
I was reading [Why Rust powers Temporal’s Core SDK](https://temporal.io/blog/why-rust-powers-core-sdk) and learned that the Core SDK serves as the foundation for the TypeScript, Python, .NET, and Ruby SDKs. I’m curious why the Java SDK isn’t built on top of the Rust Core SDK—are there technical limitations or business considerations behind this choice?

We’ve faced similar challenges as mentioned in the article and are interested in trying this approach. Since we also want to support a Java SDK, we’d love to hear any lessons learned or considerations when building a Java SDK on top of the Rust Core SDK.

comments.body:
Interestingly, the same answers for Go also apply to Java: https://github.com/temporalio/sdk-go/issues/2182. That we already had a pure Java impl by the time Rust Core came about (which would necessitate us maintaining 2 Java versions forever), and that Java has a bad native compilation and shared library distribution story.

You could say Temporal was lucky in its timing/ordering that the two worst runtimes for native library building/compilation and packaging/distribution are the ones we happen to have already had pure implementations for.

(closing issue as not an issue, feel free to join us on the #java-sdk channel on [Slack](https://t.mp/slack) or [the forum](https://community.temporal.io/).

title: Decisions behind Java SDK not using Rust Core SDK
